o1.biggest_strength: It catches the three big signals: the paused winning creator ad, the Women 25-34 pocket, and the Razor Starter Kit COD/RTO trap, with mostly correct rupee math.
o1.biggest_mistake: It says the Shopify-adjusted safe line matters, but then still holds or scales spend above that line, especially ASC/Beard/retargeting, so the rules are a bit softer than the numbers justify.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the 72% Shopify haircut the actual decision basis, not just a second line, and tighten the scale gates accordingly.

o2.biggest_strength: It makes hard budget calls on Shopify-adjusted, after-RTO economics and puts the right Monday actions first: relaunch the paused winner, cut the COD trap, and split Women 25-34.
o2.biggest_mistake: The budget plan is a little too conservative and slightly confusing, with a large unspent amount plus a reserve, and the creative note about Rohan ordering COD is the wrong behaviour to encourage.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Clean up the budget release plan so the team knows exactly how to spend or hold the full fortnight budget, and remove any ad direction that normalises COD for the starter kit.

reason: I would pay for Output 2 because it is more disciplined on the real store economics instead of Meta-reported purchases. Output 1 is very usable and more complete operationally, but it weakens its own safe-line logic when allocating budget.
